text: The Springfield Doughnut is a pink doughnut sculpture with sprinkles situated in Springfield, New Zealand. It is inspired by the doughnut commonly seen in the American animated sitcom The Simpsons, which is set in a city also named Springfield. The sculpture was donated to the town by 20th Century Fox to promote the 2007 film The Simpsons Movie. The original version, made from polystyrene encased in fibreglass, was first unveiled in July 2007 and had a diameter of 3.5 metres (11 ft) and weighed 6 tonnes (5.9 long tons; 6.6 short tons). It received a resource consent allowing it to remain for only six weeks. In September 2009, an arsonist set the sculpture on fire, destroying it. This incident occurred on the same day as consent hearings about whether the sculpture should stay permanently, leading to suspicion that the attacker was opposed to the doughnut, viewing it as a degradation of the landscape or believing Springfield should not associate with American cartoons depicting dysfunctional families. In response, local residents painted a tractor tyre pink and tan, removed a "bite" from it, and added sprinkles to replace the destroyed sculpture. On 1 July 2012, a new replacement was unveiled, constructed from concrete, with the same dimensions and weight—3.5 metres (11 ft) in diameter and 6 tonnes (5.9 long tons; 6.6 short tons). This version is fireproof and includes steps that allow people to take photos with their heads poking through the center. Between 2020 and 2023, due to flaking and falling paint, the sculpture was repainted four times at a cost of $17,864.
